title: Adaptive KV-eviction + soft-fallback orchestration for OOM mitigation
creator: Priya Nandakumar
description:
Problem: Recently seen OOM incidents under mixed burst workloads when continuous batching combines large prefixes with long-generation requests. Current safeguards (global memory cap + static eviction) cause hard failures or aggressive quality regressions. Goal: implement an adaptive memory management and graceful degradation orchestration that prevents GPU OOMs and recovers with minimal customer impact.

Proposal summary: 1) Introduce a per-request memory estimator and admission controller that predicts peak GPU working set (model weights + KV + activation estimates) before admitting a batch. 2) Implement an adaptive KV-eviction policy (prefix-aware weighted LRU) that preserves hot prefixes and evicts low-impact entries when pressure is detected. 3) Add a soft-fallback orchestration layer that enables:  a) automatic retries with exponential backoff into a lighter model variant (quantized or CPU-accelerated) when memory pressure prevents serving on preferred GPU backend, and b) truncated/partial response paths with structured reason codes when full generation cannot be guaranteed. 4) Expose runtime knobs and new metrics to Console for rollout and alerting.

Technical details: - Memory accounting: instrument the runtime to produce per-request estimates for KV size, activation peak, and workspace growth with margin. Use historical samples per model and sequence-length histogram to bias estimates. - KV eviction: implement a weighted eviction score: score = alpha * (last_used_seconds) + beta * (usage_weight) + gamma * (prefix_similarity_score). Tune alpha/beta/gamma via offline trace replay. Provide a retention window for prefixes seen in the last N minutes. - Admission controller: simulate batch admission by summing estimated peaks across coalesced requests; if predicted peak > safety_threshold, attempt progressive mitigations in order:   1) apply KV eviction; 2) reduce batch join window for low-priority requests; 3) spawn fallback path to quantized model or CPU path; 4) if none possible, return graceful truncation with retry tokens. - Soft-fallback ordering: prefer model variants with minimal quality delta per-customer config; maintain fallback chains in product config (e.g., gptx-16q → gptx-8q → gptx-cpu). - Observability: emit events for admission decisions, eviction actions (evicted byte count, prefixes evicted), fallback activations, and final response reason codes. Add histogram of predicted_vs_actual_peak to help tuning.

Trade-offs and risks: - Evicting KV harms generation quality for users with long conversational contexts; retention heuristics need careful tuning. - Admission controller conservative estimates may increase latency at tail if many requests placed into fallback. - Fallbacks to CPU or smaller models increase cost and latency; must be gated by policy and SLO. - Complexity increases runtime code surface and rollout plan must be gradual with canaries.

Rollout plan (phases): 1) Design/spec PR and config schema (2 weeks). 2) Prototype eviction + instrumentation in runtime (bench microbench) (3 weeks). 3) Offline trace replay and parameter tuning (1 week). 4) Canary behind flag for 5% traffic + dashboard and alerting (2 weeks). 5) Gradual ramp + postmortem review and playbook updates.

Links: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Adaptive+KV+Eviction+and+Soft+Fallbacks - Trace replay harness: https://git.redwood.ai/runtime/kv-evict-trace-replay - PR: https://git.redwood.ai/runtime/pull/1298 - Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/runtime-oom-mitigation
acceptance_criteria: No new GPU OOM incidents in 72h soak at 2x production QPS during canary traffic with feature enabled
Eviction events emit metrics and can be filtered in Console; retention/eviction counts are visible per-model-route
Fallback activations include a reason_code and were routed successfully with retry-backoff, verified by integration tests
Latency and token-cost regressions for P95 remain within configured SLOs or have documented compensating controls
End-to-end test: synthetic long-prefix + long-gen workload yields graceful truncated response with reason_code when fallback limits reached
